case_name: Bhagwati Prasad v State of Madhya Pradesh
respondent:
State of Madhya Pradesh
Supreme Court of India

3 December 2009
Cr.A. No. 1368 of 2003
The Judgment was delivered by : V. S. Sirpukar, J.
1. Appellant herein, who was original accused No. 6 (A-6) in the trial, has challenged the judgment of the High Court, allowing the State's Appeal and setting aside the judgment of acquittal passed by the Trial Court. All the accused persons were tried for the offences punishable u/ss. 148 and 149 read with S. 302 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (hereinafter called "IPC" or short), while the charge against the present appellant was substantively for the offence u/ss. 148 and 302 IPC.

facts: Appellant, Bhagwati Prasad, challenged the judgment of the High Court allowing the State's appeal and setting aside the judgment of acquittal passed by the Trial Court.

The allegation was that all the accused persons, six in number, formed an unlawful assembly and by way of a common object thereof, committed murder of one Ramgopal (deceased) on 18.2.1984 at about 7 A.M.

The prosecution story was that a report came to be lodged by one Kedar Prasad (PW-2) of Bansipura, the brother of Ramgopal (deceased), in Police Station Ambah to the effect that he alongwith the deceased and neighbour farmer Ramgopal (PW-3) S/o Tularam had gone to irrigate their field from the canal in Village Lahdaria situated at a distance of 12 K.M.

When they opened the canal for irrigation, at that time, Bhagwati (appellant herein), armed with spear and the other accused persons armed with Lathi came there and stopped them from opening the canal.
issues: Whether the Trial Court's acquittal of all the accused persons was correct or not
Whether the High Court's decision to set aside the acquittal and convict the appellant was justified
petitioner_arguments: The defence argued that there was no direct evidence for common object
The defence claimed that the two eye-witnesses, namely, Kedar Prasad (PW-2) and Ramgopal (PW-3), were relations and their evidence was liable to be rejected
respondent_arguments: The prosecution argued that the traumatic and homicidal death of deceased was proved
The prosecution claimed that the medical evidence, including the post-mortem report, supported the prosecution's case
court_reasoning: The High Court found that all the comments made by the Sessions Judge were completely unwarranted, irrelevant and unnecessary for the decision of the case
The High Court rejected the claim of the defence that the two eye-witnesses were relations and their evidence was liable to be rejected
The High Court concluded that the Trial Court had over-emphasized on the issue of the place of occurrence
holding: The High Court set aside the acquittal passed by the Trial Court and convicted the appellant
The High Court acquitted Devi Prasad (A-5), Hari Shankar (A-2) and Radhacharan (A-3)
cases_cited: Court relied on the decisions in Rachamreddi Chenna Reddy Vs. State of A
Lilaram (Dead) through Duli Chand Vs. State of Haryana &
